Hydrocephalus is fluid retention in the skull. It usually requires a shunt surgery to relieve the pressure to keep the skull from growing and becoming essentially deformed. It can cause mental disability and mental retardation in some cases. I had a friend at the children's hospital when I was sick. He was a janitor and his name was Charlie. He had hydrocephalus as a child and thus had a slightly larger skull than average. He was a bit below cognitively but he was super nice. I loved getting to see him each night when he collected the trash from each room. He'd tell me about growing up in Tennessee, and his childhood medical crap that he had to deal with too (it was nice to know he knew how I felt) A friend of my mom's owns a chocolate shop, and gave us a bunch of little individual boxes of chocolates for the docs and nurses and stuff for Christmas. We made sure all my nurses got one as well as Charlie and all my CNAs. When Charlie retired I was really sad, but Stanley who took over was super nice. His son had chronic asthma and often was in the hospital. He loved balloons. So whenever I had a bunch of balloons that people sent and I was discharged, I'd let Stanley know and he'd get them refilled at the gift shop and bring them home for his son. It was really cute. 😊
